text:
tanya: quick heads-up — I brought up the new model (redwood-rev1) in the staging pool. goal: quick quant smoke + accuracy-delta checks for AWQ / GPTQ / INT8 / FP8 before we open a canary for hosted.
kevin: good. start with a 100-sample eval (MMLU subset + LAMBADA + 50 safety prompts). collect latency + per-sample logprobs. keep batches small (seq len ~ 512).
maria: ran the 100-sample sweep this morning. results (baseline fp16): MMLU 71.4, LAMBADA 62.1. AWQ (4-bit) -> MMLU 69.6 (-1.8), LAMBADA 60.3 (-1.8). GPTQ (int8) -> MMLU 70.9 (-0.5), LAMBADA 61.6 (-0.5). INT8 (per-channel) -> MMLU 70.1 (-1.3). FP8 (experimental kernel) -> MMLU 71.0 (-0.4) but unstable on long contexts.
samira: thanks. any heavy tail failures (hallucination spikes or token degeneracy) in AWQ or FP8?
maria: AWQ had 2 prompts with repetition loops at 1e-3 prob threshold. FP8 had 1 occasion where token probs collapsed after 1.2k tokens — only in the long-context sim.
oliver: cost/latency numbers? we need to decide tradeoffs for hosted vs dedicated.
maria: AWQ p50 latency 85ms, GPTQ int8 p50 95ms, fp16 baseline p50 120ms. Cost per token AWQ ~0.65x baseline, GPTQ ~0.72x. FP8 throughput looks great but kernel fallback increased tail latency on some nodes.
kevin: for an initial hosted canary i'd prefer GPTQ as the primary quant target (best accuracy delta, decent perf). AWQ as secondary for cost-sensitive customers, but we need a strict fallback for the repetition/regression cases.
tanya: agreed. proposal for rollout config (canary + automated fallback):
```yaml
canary:
  percent: 5
  duration_minutes: 120
  metrics:
    - name: avg_latency_p95
      threshold_ms: 300
    - name: avg_mmlu_delta
      threshold_pct: -1.0
fallback_order:
  - variant: gptq-int8
  - variant: fp16
  - variant: awq-4bit
  - variant: fp8-experimental
health_checks:
  sample_eval_set: staging_100
  anomaly_window_minutes: 10
  rollback_on_quality_drop: true
```
ryan: small nit — fallback order should prefer accuracy before cost for hosted. so fallback to fp16 before gptq-int8? our earlier numbers show GPTQ was closer to baseline than fp16? double-check.
maria: we measured fp16 as baseline. GPTQ int8 was actually slightly better than awq but slightly worse than fp16. reorder to prefer fp16 first. updated fallback: [fp16, gptq-int8, awq-4bit].
deploy-bot: [1765555600] Canary start: redwood-rev1@gptq-int8 -> 5% hosted traffic. monitors: latency, error-rate, eval-metrics.
tanya: watching MMLU delta window. if avg_mmlu_delta <= -1.0% over 30m -> auto-fallback to fp16 and create incident.
oliver: for Dedicated pools we should allow AWQ as default (customers willing to sacrifice a bit of accuracy for cost) but expose a per-customer override. fallback there should be to gptq-int8 then fp16.
kevin: private (VPC) deploys: require opt-in for experimental FP8 kernels. default to fp16/gptq only. ensure we ship kernel blacklist for older GPUs.
maria: one more item — add a small regression test harness that runs 200 seed prompts within the canary window and fails the rollout if >1.5% MMLU drop or any hallucination score above threshold.
tanya: action items: 1) kevin to update canary config and reorder fallback. 2) maria to extend smoke harness with hallucination check + long-context stress tests. 3) ops to add kernel blacklist for FP8 on pre-Ampere nodes. 4) samira to draft a customer-facing note for Dedicated/private differences.
samira: will draft note and ping legal if wording mentions stability guarantees.
deploy-bot: [1765555615] Canary health ok for first 30m. no rollbacks triggered yet.
ryan: keep logs and eval snapshots for >=7 days — we need them if we see slow drifting regressions.
tanya: thanks everyone. we’ll reconvene after the 2h canary. if any major quality regressions pop up we trigger immediate fallback to fp16 and open a postmortem.
kevin: +1
oliver: +1 :thumbsup:
